messages:
maria: Heads up — staging p99 for the rg-3b-v2 onboarding climbed ~3x right after the onboarding merge. Canary flagged at 05:12 UTC. Anyone else seeing this?

kevin: Yep, I noticed the spike around 05:10. Reproducer in perf/regression/rg-3b-v2/short-chat. Metrics: batch sizes collapse, KV evictions spike.

jen: Running a quick perf profile on a failing canary instance now, attaching top hotspots (trimmed):
```
[perf-summary]
0.45 runtime::kv_cache::evict
0.30 kernel::avx_fused_attention
0.15 scheduler::batch_pick
0.05 allocator::alloc_spin
```
Batch size distribution -> median 1, p95=4 (was median 8).

maria: Interesting — I also see many short prompts tokenizing to more tokens than before. We onboarded a tokenizer normalization change in that PR; could be inflating seq lengths for the short-chat traffic. KV cache thrash due to shorter batches + more unique prefixes?

kevin: I diffed the tokenizer map: the normalization adds explicit normalization for whitespace sequences and a new fallback split which increases token count for lines starting with "Q:" and short system prompts. That pushes avg seq_len up from ~14 -> ~29 for a subset of traffic.

jen: Bisect started. Primary suspects: tokenizer-normalize (commit 2ad4f7) vs kernel-route-change (commit 8b3c2f). Running an isolated build with tokenizer revert.

perf-bot: CI perf check failed: staging-checks #4821 — rg-3b-v2 p99 latency +210% vs baseline.

maria: This is a rollout blocker, please hold further canaries. @kevin can you open a revert?

kevin: Opening revert PR for tokenizer normalization in shadow path now. Also preparing a short-lived policy tweak to prefer the latency-optimized kernel for seq_len < 40 while we investigate. PRs: #2728 (revert), #2730 (kernel-selector hack).

jen: Quick note from profiling: scheduler's seq_len_mu used by kernel selector shifted from ~16 -> ~34 in the failing runs, which flipped the selector threshold (we use seq_len_threshold: 24). That caused requests to be scheduled to a kernel variant that doesn't use prefix-friendly caching (prefetch disabled), making kvcache effectiveness drop.

kevin: Applied revert to staging -> deploy-bot rolled canary back at 06:05 UTC.

deploy-bot: Rolled back canary for rg-3b-v2 to previous image (sha: a1b2c3) — action triggered by #2728.

jen: After revert, p99 returned to baseline in the canary runs. Confirmed hotpath: tokenizer increased tokens -> scheduler picks different kernel -> kvcache eviction rate increased -> cold-start for many seqs -> latency spike.

maria: TL;DR: tokenizer normalization unintentionally changed sequence length distribution; kernel-selector thresholds + kernel fallback semantics made the effect much worse by choosing a kernel path with poor prefix/KV cache behavior.

kevin: Proposed follow-ups (short):
- revert tokenizer normalization from onboarding branch (done)
- add unit test that tracks token count distribution for short-chat testset during tokenizer onboarding
- make kernel selector use smoothed seq_len metric (exponential moving avg) instead of instant mu to avoid flip-flops
- add kvcache eviction alarms tied to scheduler kernel routes
- update onboarding checklist to run a lightweight staging perf harness before canary

jen: Also adding a mitigation: temporarily prefer prefix-caching-capable kernels if kvcache evaporation rate > 5% for a minute to avoid full thrash loops. Will draft change.

maria: Good. Can someone add action items in the incident board and link here? I'll do the postmortem once the PRs land.

kevin: Adding tasks to the sprint board and will follow up with the test coverage PR.

perf-bot: Marking thread as incident: perf-regression (severity: P2) — followup required.

maria: Thanks all — great quick catch. We'll keep the rollout paused until the stabilization changes land. :thumbsup:
